title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 4 Lesson 2: Angled Friction And Rings custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A ring of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough vertical wire where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.4$. A horizontal force of magnitude $P$ presses the ring against the wire. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the minimum value of $P$ required to prevent the ring from sliding downwards.

A ring of mass $0.8\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough vertical rod. A string pulls the ring with a tension of $20\text{ N}$ directed at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the upward vertical. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the rod on the ring.

A ring of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ ($W = 6\text{ N}$) is threaded on a rough vertical rod with $\mu = 0.5$. An angled force pulls the ring such that the normal reaction is $R = 14\text{ N}$ and the upward vertical component of the pull is $11\text{ N}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the magnitude and direction of the friction force acting on the ring.

A block of mass $19\text{ kg}$ rests on rough horizontal ground with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.25$. A rope pulls the block with tension $T$ at an angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$ (so $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$). Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the tension $T$ when the block is in limiting equilibrium.

A ring of mass $1.2\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough vertical wire where $\mu = 0.25$. A horizontal force provides a constant normal reaction of $R = 16\text{ N}$. A vertical upward pulling force $P$ is applied to the ring. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the maximum value $P_{\max}$ for which the ring remains at rest.

A ring of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough horizontal rod where $\mu = 0.5$. A force of magnitude $10\text{ N}$ pushes the ring at an angle of $30^\circ$ below the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the rod on the ring and the maximum static frictional force $F_{\max}$.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $m = 300\text{ kg}$ rests on rough horizontal ground where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.5$. A pulling force of magnitude $X$ acts on the crate at an angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = 0.28$ (and $\cos\alpha = 0.96$). The crate is in limiting equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 3000\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving vertically, express the normal reaction $R$ in terms of $X$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By setting up the horizontal limiting equilibrium equation, calculate the value of $X$ correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $m$ rests on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.3$. A force of magnitude $50\text{ N}$ pushes the block at an angle of $20^\circ$ below the horizontal, causing it to slide at a constant speed. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By considering vertical forces in equilibrium, express the normal reaction $R$ in terms of $m$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving horizontally for motion at constant speed, calculate the mass $m$ of the block correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A ring of mass $m = 0.5\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough fixed vertical rod where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.35$. A light string pulls the ring with tension $T$ at an angle of $40^\circ$ above the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 5\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If the ring is on the point of slipping upwards, calculate the tension $T_1$ in the string correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If instead the ring is on the point of slipping downwards, calculate the tension $T_2$ in the string correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A ring $R$ of mass $m = 1.5\text{ kg}$ ($W = 15\text{ N}$) is threaded on a rough vertical wire where $\mu = 0.4$. Two light strings $AR$ and $BR$ pull the ring: string $AR$ pulls at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal with tension $T_A = 20\text{ N}$, and string $BR$ pulls at $45^\circ$ below the horizontal with tension $T_B$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that the horizontal forces exerted by the strings balance exactly so that the wire exerts no normal reaction on the ring ($R = 0$), determine the value of $T_B$ and find the resultant downward vertical force acting on the ring.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the friction force in this state is zero ($F_f = 0$), and calculate the initial vertical acceleration of the ring.

questions.prompt: A ring of mass $m = 0.8\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough fixed horizontal rod where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.5$. A light string pulls the ring with tension $T$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal ($0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$). Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 8\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If $T = 6\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 30^\circ$, calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the rod on the ring and find the maximum static friction $F_{\max}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that when $T = 6\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 30^\circ$, the ring cannot remain in equilibrium and will accelerate along the rod.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the tension $T_0$ such that the ring is in limiting equilibrium when pulled at an angle of $\theta = 45^\circ$ above the horizontal.

questions.prompt: A ring of mass $M = 2\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough vertical pole where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.6$. A pulling force of magnitude $P$ is applied to the ring at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 20\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine the minimum force $P_{\min}$ required to prevent the ring from sliding downwards, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why it is impossible to make the ring slide upwards by increasing the magnitude of $P$ at this angle, and state the complete range of values of $P$ for which the ring remains in equilibrium.

questions.prompt: A ring $A$ of mass $m_A = 0.4\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough fixed horizontal rod where $\mu = 0.75$. A light inextensible string attached to ring $A$ passes over a small smooth pulley $P$ fixed at a vertical height $h = 0.8\text{ m}$ above the rod. The other end of the string supports a suspended mass $B$ of mass $m_B = 1.3\text{ kg}$ ($W_B = 13\text{ N}$). Ring $A$ is held at a horizontal distance $x$ from the vertical line passing through $P$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W_A = 4\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: When $x = 0.6\text{ m}$, find the tension $T$ in the string, and show that the normal reaction exerted by the rod on ring $A$ is $R = 6.4\text{ N}$ acting vertically downwards.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When $x = 0.6\text{ m}$, determine whether ring $A$ remains in equilibrium or slides towards the pulley.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Determine the angle $\theta$ of the string to the horizontal when ring $A$ is in limiting equilibrium on the verge of sliding towards the pulley, and find the corresponding horizontal distance $x$ correct to 3 significant figures.
